MARKING SCHEME
SECTION A (30 MARKS)
(a) Definition of “Inspired”
The term inspired means that the writers of the Bible were guided by the Holy Spirit to write God’s message without
error.
(b) Two human authors of the Bible
i. Moses
ii. Paul
(c) Why the Bible is called a “Library”
Because it is made up of many books written by different authors, at different times, and in different styles.
(a) Categories of Old Testament books
Learner Category described
Wanjiku Law (Pentateuch)
Achieng Major Prophets
Kiplagat Poetry (Wisdom books)
Mutua Historical books
(b)
Kiplagat
(a)
The Fall of Man (Adam and Eve disobeying God)
(b) Two consequences of sin
i. Separation from God
ii. Death and suffering entered the world
(c) Redemption
Redemption is the act of saving humans from sin through Jesus Christ.
(a)
Environmental conservation / Stewardship of creation
(b)
FALSE
(c) Two qualities of a good steward
i. Responsible
ii. Faithful
(a)
Moses
(b)
God’s power / Judgment / Justice
(c) Difference between Passover Lamb and Jesus Christ
The Passover lamb was sacrificed to save Israelites from physical death, while Jesus Christ is the Lamb of God who
was sacrificed to save humanity from sin and eternal death.
(a)
Stone tablets
(b)
They worshipped the golden calf (idolatry)
(c) Renewal of Sinai Covenant
 • Moses made new stone tablets
 • God rewrote the commandments
 • Israelites repented and renewed their commitment
 • Sacrifices were offered
 • The covenant relationship with God was restored
SECTION B (50 MARKS)
(a)
Mount Carmel
(b) Reasons Elijah contested prophets of Baal
i. To prove that Yahweh is the true God
ii. To stop idol worship
iv. To expose false prophets
(c) Circumstances leading to Elijah’s flight
i. Queen Jezebel threatened to kill him
ii. Fear for his life
iii. He became discouraged
iv. He fled into the wilderness
(d) Forms of idol worship today
i. Worship of money (materialism)
ii. Occult practices
iii. False prophets / cults
(a)
Idol worship/Idolatry
(b) Religious background during Amos’ time
i. People practiced idol worship
ii. There was hypocrisy in worship
iii. Religious leaders were corrupt
iv. People ignored God’s laws
(c) “Day of the Lord” (Amos)
It is a day of judgment when God punishes sin and injustice, not a day of joy as people expected.
(d) Remnant vs Restoration
 • Remnant: A small faithful group that remains after judgment
 • Restoration: God rebuilding and blessing His people after punishment
(a)
Bethlehem
(b) Role of John the Baptist
i. Prepared the way for Jesus
ii. Called people to repentance
iii. Baptized believers
iv. Identified Jesus as the Messiah
(c) Relevance of Jesus’ baptism
i. Shows obedience to God
ii. Symbol of repentance
iii. Example for Christians
iv. Marks beginning of Christian life
(d) Temptations of Jesus
i. Turning stones into bread
ii. Jumping from the temple
iii. Worshipping Satan

(a)
Irresponsible sexual behavior / Peer pressure/Drug and substance abuse
(b) Dating vs Courtship
 • Dating: Casual relationship mainly for social purposes
 • Courtship: Serious relationship with intention of marriage, guided by Christian values
(c) Christian teaching on relationships (Genesis 1:26–28)
i. Men and women are equal before God
ii. They should respect each other
iii. They are to multiply responsibly
iv. They should live in harmony
(d) Solutions to irresponsible sexual behavior
i. Sex education and guidance
ii. Strong Christian values
iii. Parental guidance
iv. Avoiding peer pressure
